title: Converting Between Blocks and Proc Objects
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of converting between blocks and proc objects in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply converting between blocks and proc objects in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to block forwarding and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Converting Between Blocks and Proc Objects through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding converting between blocks and proc objects helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Converting Between Blocks and Proc Objects helps you reason about the & operator. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: The & operator. Then connect it to Passing callable objects. The remaining syllabus points—Block forwarding—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports converting between blocks and proc objects. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.text: Create a second example for converting between blocks and proc objects using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Block forwarding), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain converting between blocks and proc objects, identify its place in blocks, procs, lambdas, and closures, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
